original_text: After adverse evidence, the accused is invited to make a statement but is not obliged to do so
rationale: The India Code compilation of r.23(3) prints the caution as 'You are obliged to say anything unless you wish to do so' (no 'not'); both MML DOC copies print 'You are not obliged to say anything...'. original_text:
any voluntary statement is recorded and read over. The accused is not cross-examined on that statement at this stage and may call defence or character witnesses.

proposed_text: Optional precision: state that this is the summary-of-evidence stage under AR r.23 (not the CO's hearing under r.22), and that under r.23(4) the statement is recorded in English and interpreted to the accused in a language he understands.

claim: Custody/detention/confinement under s.80 are not awardable to NCOs.
original_text: Check Section 81 restrictions: e.g., custody/detention/confinement are not awardable to NCOs; reprimand is not for ranks below NCO.
proposed_text: Proposal: 'Under s.81(4), punishments in s.80(a), (b) and (c) cannot be awarded to a person who is an NCO, or who was an NCO when the offence was committed. Under s.81(5), s.80(g) (severe reprimand or reprimand) cannot be awarded below NCO rank.'
rationale: s.81(4) bars s.80(a)-(c) for a person 'who is of the rank of non-commissioned officer or was, at the time of committing the offence for which he is punished, of such rank'. The record omits the second limb, so a person reduced from NCO rank after the offence could wrongly be treated as eligible for imprisonment in military custody, detention or confinement. The reprimand bar (s.81(5)) is stated correctly. Severity P1 because the omitted condition concerns lawfulness of a custodial summary punishment.

claim: Three-year limitation for commencing court-martial trial, starting from offence/knowledge/identity; exceptions for desertion, fraudulent enrolment and s.37 offences; excluded periods; s.122(4) qualification.
original_text: The normal limitation is three years, subject to rules on commencement tied to date of offence, knowledge or known identity; statutory exceptions cover desertion, fraudulent enrolment and Section 37 offences, and particular periods are excluded.
rationale: s.122(1)(a)-(c), (2), (3) and (4) on [[page 35]] match: three years from (a) date of offence, (b) first knowledge of the aggrieved person or competent authority, whichever earlier, or (c) first knowledge of identity, whichever earlier; (2) excludes desertion, fraudulent enrolment and s.37 offences; (3) excludes time as POW, in enemy territory or evading arrest; (4) bars trial for desertion (other than on active service) or fraudulent enrolment after three years' exemplary continuous service by a non-officer. 'Do not assume a CoI or SoE pauses limitation' is consistent with s.122(3) listing only those exclusions.

claim: Computation guidance relies only on s.122(1)-(4), framed as 'apply the earliest relevant knowledge rule'.
original_text: Apply the earliest relevant knowledge rule in Section 122(1). Test Section 122(2) exceptions and (3)/(4) qualifications separately.
proposed_text: Proposal: 'Identify which limb of s.122(1) applies on the facts: (a) date of offence; (b) where the offence was not known, the earlier of first knowledge by the person aggrieved or the competent authority; (c) where the offender was unknown, the earlier date on which identity became known to either. If the accused has ceased to be subject to the Act, also apply s.123(2) (trial must commence within three years of ceasing to be subject, with stated exclusions; proviso for desertion, fraudulent enrolment and s.37 offences).'
rationale: (i) 'Earliest relevant knowledge rule' is imprecise: 'whichever is earlier' in s.122(1)(b)-(c) compares the aggrieved person and the competent authority within the applicable limb; it does not authorise choosing the earliest of limbs (a)-(c). (ii) The record omits s.123(2), a separate three-year bar running from the date a person ceased to be subject to the Act, with its own exclusions and proviso. A court-martial convened on a chronology that ignores s.123 could be time-barred. Court-martial jurisdiction content: P1.
pinpoint: Army Act s.122(1)(a)-(c) and s.123(1)-(2) with proviso, India Code compilation [[page 35]]
temporal_scope: Army Act 1950 as consolidated on India Code (retrieved 2026-11-21); amendments after that date and original Gazette text not verified.

claim: s.14 governs service-matter applications; s.15 gives appellate jurisdiction over court-martial orders/findings/sentences with powers on conviction, sentence and bail; relief within s.15(4)-(6) including enhancement after hearing; SCM dismissal needs analysis under ss.3(o), 14, 15.
original_text: Section 14 governs service-matter applications. Section 15 provides appellate jurisdiction over an order, decision, finding or sentence passed by court-martial, with specified powers over conviction, sentence and bail.
rationale: AFT Act s.14(1)-(2) [[page 8]] confers jurisdiction over service matters on application by an aggrieved person. s.15(1)-(2) [[page 9]] confers appellate jurisdiction over 'any order, decision, finding or sentence passed by a court-martial'; s.15(3) bail (with proviso for death/life offences); s.15(4)-(6) grounds and powers; s.15(6)(c) with proviso [[page 10]] permits enhancement only after hearing the appellant. s.3(o)(iii) includes 'summary disposal and trials where the punishment of dismissal is awarded' in service matters, while exclusion (iv) removes SCMs except where punishment is dismissal or imprisonment over three months - supporting the record's SCM-dismissal example.

claim: BNSS s.521 provides for Central Government rules on forum allocation and delivery to commanding officers; BNSS s.521 alone does not give a CO forum-choice power; pending matters depend on pre/post 1-7-2024.
original_text: BNSS section 521 provides for Central Government rules governing trial forum allocation and delivery to military commanding officers in appropriate cases.
rationale: BNSS s.521(1) [[page 172]] empowers the Central Government to make rules on which persons subject to army, naval or air-force law are tried by a criminal court or court-martial, and requires a Magistrate to have regard to those rules and in proper cases deliver the accused to the commanding officer. The red flag 'Assuming BNSS 521 alone grants CO forum-choice power' is supported: the choice is vested by Army Act s.125 in the officer commanding the army, army corps, division or independent brigade (or prescribed officer), with s.126 governing criminal-court requisition. BNSS s.531(2)(a) [[page 174]] preserves CrPC for proceedings pending on commencement, consistent with the 'before or after 1 July 2024' check.
temporal_scope: BNSS as on India Code (retrieved 2026-11-21), commencement 1-7-2024 per corpus metadata; Army Act consolidation retrieved 2026-11-21.
limitations: CrPC s.475 text only partially read from poor OCR (S-BLIND-011).
